contentObjective: I can compare ratios by finding unit rates or using equivalent ratios.
languageObjective: I can explain my comparison using the words unit rate, equivalent ratio, compare, and common denominator.

vocabulary.definition: Decide which ratio is greater, less, or equal by using equivalent ratios or unit rates.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Decidir cuál razón es mayor, menor o igual usando razones equivalentes o tasas unitarias.
vocabulary.cloze: Make the ___ match, or find each ___ ___, before deciding which ratio is greater.

examples.why: Both reduced to the same unit.
Different quantities, so the totals say nothing.

vocabulary.definition: A rate for just 1 of something, like cost for 1 item.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tasa para solo 1 de algo, como el precio de 1 artículo.
vocabulary.cloze: A rate that tells the amount for exactly one unit, like 5 miles per 1 hour, is a ___.

examples.why: The amount for exactly one unit.
A rate for three, not one.

vocabulary.definition: Two ratios that mean the same thing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos razones que significan lo mismo.

steps: 1. Convert each ratio to a unit rate (e.g. price per item or miles per gallon)
2. Alternatively, scale both ratios to a common term (like a common denominator)
3. Compare the resulting unit rates to identify the better buy or faster rate

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Babysitting Pay
revealWordProblem.text:
Claire, Yuzuki, and Nakai compared the hours they babysat last weekend and what they were paid, shown on the calendar. A new family is looking for a babysitter and is offering $10.75 per hour.
Question: Who would want to take this offer, based on what they were paid the previous weekend?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Three calendar days showing each student's babysitting hours and pay: Claire 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. for $31.50, Yuzuki 12 p.m. to 8 p.m. for $63, Nakai 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. for $50.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Find each unit rate in dollars per hour. Claire worked 3 hours for $31.50, so $31.50 ÷ 3 = $10.50 per hour. Yuzuki worked 8 hours for $63, so $63 ÷ 8 = $7.875 per hour. Nakai worked 4 hours for $50, so $50 ÷ 4 = $12.50 per hour. The offer is $10.75 per hour. Claire ($10.50) and Yuzuki ($7.88) would both earn more than before, so they would want the offer. Nakai already earns $12.50 per hour, so the offer would be a pay cut for him.

questions.stem: Chef A uses 2 cups of cheese for every 8 crackers. Chef B uses 3 cups of cheese for every 9 crackers. Who uses more cheese per cracker?
questions.explanation: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 cups per cracker. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 cups per cracker. Chef B uses more cheese per cracker.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Chef A: 2÷8 = ___ cups per cracker.
The two ratios do not reduce to the same value, so they are not equal. Divide each cheese amount by its cracker count and compare the results.
You have both amounts, so a comparison is possible. Turn each ratio into cheese per cracker and the answer appears.
hints: You can't compare 2 cups and 3 cups directly — the chefs use different numbers of crackers.
Find each chef's cheese for ONE cracker: divide cheese by crackers for each, then compare the two rates.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compare those two decimals to see who uses more per cracker.
questions.stemEs: El chef A usa 2 tazas de queso por cada 8 galletas saladas. El chef B usa 3 tazas de queso por cada 9 galletas saladas. ¿Quién usa más queso por galleta?
questions.explanationEs: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 tazas por galleta. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 tazas por galleta. El chef B usa más queso por galleta.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar 2 tazas y 3 tazas directamente: los chefs usan cantidades distintas de galletas.
Halla el queso de cada chef para UNA galleta: divide queso entre galletas en cada caso y luego compara las dos tasas.
Chef A: divide 2 ÷ 8. Chef B: divide 3 ÷ 9. Compara esos dos decimales para ver quién usa más por galleta.

questions.explanation: Convert to the same denominator: 3:4 = 6:8. Since 6:8 > 5:8, the ratio 3:4 is greater.
choiceFeedback: Compare the ratios carefully — which one is greater?
Rewrite both ratios with the same second number before deciding — scale the first ratio so its second term is 8, then compare.
Both ratios are exact numbers, so they can be compared. Scale one of them until the second terms match.
hints: The second numbers (4 and 8) don't match, so the ratios aren't ready to compare yet.
Rewrite the ratios with the same second number — 8 works nicely, since 4 × 2 = 8 — then compare the first numbers.
Scale 3:4 by 2: multiply both parts to get an out-of-8 ratio. Then compare its first number with the 5 in 5:8.
questions.explanationEs: Convierte a un denominador común: 3:4 = 6:8. Como 6:8 > 5:8, la razón 3:4 es mayor.
hintsEs: Los segundos números (4 y 8) no coinciden, así que las razones todavía no están listas para compararse.
Reescribe las razones con el mismo segundo número —el 8 funciona bien, porque 4 × 2 = 8— y luego compara los primeros números.
Escala 3:4 por 2: multiplica ambas partes para obtener una razón sobre 8. Luego compara su primer número con el 5 de 5:8.

questions.stem: Which lemonade recipe is more lemony? Recipe A: 2 lemons for 6 cups of water. Recipe B: 3 lemons for 7 cups of water.
questions.explanation: Recipe A: 2÷6 ≈ 0.33 lemons per cup. Recipe B: 3÷7 ≈ 0.43 lemons per cup. Since 0.43 > 0.33, Recipe B is more lemony.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Recipe A: 2÷6 ≈ 0.33 lemons per cup.
The ratios 2:6 and 3:7 do not reduce to the same value. Find the lemons per cup for each recipe and compare the decimals.
Every number you need is given. Divide lemons by cups for each recipe to compare them fairly.
hints: Recipe B has more lemons, but it also has more water — so compare rates, not raw counts.
Find lemons per ONE cup of water for each recipe: divide lemons by cups. The bigger rate is more lemony.
Recipe A: divide 2 ÷ 6. Recipe B: divide 3 ÷ 7. Compare the two decimals you get.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál receta de limonada tiene más sabor a limón? Receta A: 2 limones por 6 tazas de agua. Receta B: 3 limones por 7 tazas de agua.
questions.explanationEs: Receta A: 2÷6 ≈ 0.33 limones por taza. Receta B: 3÷7 ≈ 0.43 limones por taza. Como 0.43 > 0.33, la receta B tiene más sabor a limón.
hintsEs: La receta B tiene más limones, pero también más agua, así que compara tasas, no conteos sueltos.
Halla los limones por UNA taza de agua en cada receta: divide limones entre tazas. La tasa mayor sabe más a limón.
Receta A: divide 2 ÷ 6. Receta B: divide 3 ÷ 7. Compara los dos decimales que obtengas.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Compare Ratios is thinking the ratio with the bigger raw number automatically wins — like assuming Chef Tran's 8 tablespoons of cocoa must be more chocolatey than Chef Reyes's 6 tablespoons, without checking that the milk amounts (14 oz vs. 10 oz) are different. Never compare the raw numbers alone — always scale both ratios to the same amount or find each unit rate first.

level1.stem: Which is the better deal: 4 apples for $3 or 6 apples for $5?
level1.explanation: Deal 1: $3÷4 = $0.75 per apple. Deal 2: $5÷6 ≈ $0.83 per apple. $0.75 < $0.83, so 4 apples for $3 is the better deal.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Deal 2: $5÷6 ≈ $0.83 per apple.
The two deals do not work out to the same price per apple. Divide each price by its number of apples and compare.
You can compare these — just make them match. Find the cost of a single apple in each deal.
hints: 'Better deal' means the LOWER cost for one apple — not simply more apples.
Find the price of one apple in each deal: divide dollars by apples, then pick the smaller price.
Deal 1: divide 3 ÷ 4 to get dollars per apple. Do the same with 5 ÷ 6, then compare the two prices.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál es la mejor oferta: 4 manzanas por $3 o 6 manzanas por $5?
level1.explanationEs: Oferta 1: $3÷4 = $0.75 por manzana. Oferta 2: $5÷6 ≈ $0.83 por manzana. Como $0.75 < $0.83, 4 manzanas por $3 es la mejor oferta.
hintsEs: 'Mejor oferta' significa el MENOR costo por una manzana, no simplemente más manzanas.
Halla el precio de una manzana en cada oferta: divide dólares entre manzanas y luego escoge el precio menor.
Oferta 1: divide 3 ÷ 4 para obtener dólares por manzana. Haz lo mismo con 5 ÷ 6 y luego compara los dos precios.

level2.stem: Store A sells 3 mangoes for $6. Store B sells 5 mangoes for $9. Which store offers a better price per mango?
level2.explanation: Store A: $6÷3 = $2.00 per mango. Store B: $9÷5 = $1.80 per mango. Store B has the better (lower) price per mango.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Store A: $6÷3 = $2.00 per mango.
$6 for 3 and $9 for 5 do not give the same unit price. Divide each total by its number of mangoes to check.
Both the prices and the counts are known, so a unit price can be found for each store.
hints: The stores sell different counts for different prices — compare the price of ONE mango.
Divide dollars by mangoes for each store, then choose the store with the lower per-mango price.
Store A: divide 6 ÷ 3 for its price per mango. Store B: divide 9 ÷ 5. Compare the two prices.
level2.stemEs: La tienda A vende 3 mangos por $6. La tienda B vende 5 mangos por $9. ¿Cuál tienda ofrece mejor precio por mango?
level2.explanationEs: Tienda A: $6÷3 = $2.00 por mango. Tienda B: $9÷5 = $1.80 por mango. La tienda B tiene el mejor precio (el más bajo) por mango.
hintsEs: Las tiendas venden cantidades distintas a precios distintos: compara el precio de UN mango.
Divide dólares entre mangos en cada tienda y luego elige la tienda con el menor precio por mango.
Tienda A: divide 6 ÷ 3 para su precio por mango. Tienda B: divide 9 ÷ 5. Compara los dos precios.

level2.stem: Chef Academy's snack bar sells 3 mini quiches for $6 or 5 mini quiches for $8. Which is the better deal per quiche?
level2.explanation: 3 for $6 is $6 / 3 = $2.00 per quiche. 5 for $8 is $8 / 5 = $1.60 per quiche. $1.60 < $2.00, so 5 quiches for $8 is the better deal.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 3 for $6 is $6 / 3 = $2.00 per quiche.
The two prices do not reduce to the same cost per quiche. Divide each total by its number of quiches and compare.
Both prices and both counts are given, so a unit price can be calculated for each option.
level2.stemEs: La cafetería de la Academia de Chefs vende 3 mini quiches por $6 o 5 mini quiches por $8. ¿Cuál es la mejor oferta por quiche?
level2.explanationEs: 3 por $6 son $6 / 3 = $2.00 por quiche. 5 por $8 son $8 / 5 = $1.60 por quiche. Como $1.60 < $2.00, 5 quiches por $8 es la mejor oferta.
hints: A better deal means each single quiche costs less, not that the total price is smaller.
Find the unit price for each option: the total cost divided by the number of quiches.
The first option gives $6 ÷ 3 per quiche. Do the same division for $8 and 5 quiches, then compare the two prices.
hintsEs: Una mejor oferta significa que cada quiche cuesta menos, no que el precio total sea menor.
Encuentra el precio por unidad de cada opción: el costo total dividido entre la cantidad de quiches.
La primera opción da $6 ÷ 3 por quiche. Haz la misma división con $8 y 5 quiches y luego compara los dos precios.

level2.stem: Two soup recipes use salt. Recipe A uses 4 tsp salt for 10 cups of broth. Recipe B uses 3 tsp salt for 8 cups of broth. Which soup is saltier per cup?
level2.explanation: Recipe A: 4 / 10 = 0.4 tsp per cup. Recipe B: 3 / 8 = 0.375 tsp per cup. Since 0.4 > 0.375, Recipe A is saltier per cup.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Recipe B: 3 / 8 = ___ tsp per cup.
The fractions 4/10 and 3/8 are not equivalent. Convert each one to salt per cup as a decimal and compare.
Both the salt and the broth amounts are given, so unit rates can settle this.
level2.stemEs: Dos recetas de sopa usan sal. La receta A usa 4 cucharaditas de sal para 10 tazas de caldo. La receta B usa 3 cucharaditas de sal para 8 tazas de caldo. ¿Cuál sopa es más salada por taza?
level2.explanationEs: Receta A: 4 / 10 = 0.4 cucharaditas por taza. Receta B: 3 / 8 = 0.375 cucharaditas por taza. Como 0.4 > 0.375, la receta A es más salada por taza.
hints: Saltier per cup means more teaspoons of salt for each single cup of broth.
Divide the salt by the broth in each recipe to get teaspoons per cup.
Recipe A gives 4 ÷ 10 teaspoons per cup. Work out 3 ÷ 8 for Recipe B and compare the two decimals.
hintsEs: Más salada por taza significa más cucharaditas de sal por cada taza de caldo.
Divide la sal entre el caldo en cada receta para obtener cucharaditas por taza.
La receta A da 4 ÷ 10 cucharaditas por taza. Calcula 3 ÷ 8 para la receta B y compara los dos decimales.

level2.stem: Chef Mara's lemon glaze uses 6 oz of lemon juice for 9 cupcakes. Chef Devi's uses 4 oz for 7 cupcakes. Whose glaze has more lemon per cupcake?
level2.explanation: Chef Mara: 6 / 9 = 0.666... oz per cupcake. Chef Devi: 4 / 7 = 0.571... oz per cupcake. Since 0.67 > 0.57, Chef Mara's glaze has more lemon per cupcake.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Chef Devi: 4 / 7 = ___.
The ratios 6/9 and 4/7 do not simplify to the same value. Divide ounces by cupcakes for each chef and compare.
Both recipes give enough information — find the ounces per cupcake for each one.
level2.stemEs: El glaseado de limón de la chef Mara usa 6 oz de jugo de limón para 9 panquecitos. El de la chef Devi usa 4 oz para 7 panquecitos. ¿Cuál glaseado tiene más limón por panquecito?
level2.explanationEs: Chef Mara: 6 / 9 = 0.666... oz por panquecito. Chef Devi: 4 / 7 = 0.571... oz por panquecito. Como 0.67 > 0.57, el glaseado de la chef Mara tiene más limón por panquecito.
hints: More lemon per cupcake means a greater unit rate of ounces to cupcakes.
For each chef, divide the ounces of juice by the number of cupcakes.
Chef Mara's rate is 6 ÷ 9 and Chef Devi's is 4 ÷ 7. Write both as decimals and compare them.
hintsEs: Más limón por panquecito significa una tasa por unidad mayor de onzas por panquecito.
Para cada chef, divide las onzas de jugo entre la cantidad de panquecitos.
La tasa de la chef Mara es 6 ÷ 9 y la de la chef Devi es 4 ÷ 7. Escribe las dos como decimales y compáralas.

level2.stem: Store A sells 5 notebooks for $12. Store B sells 8 notebooks for $20. Without calculating, a student says Store B must be cheaper because you get more notebooks. Is the student's reasoning valid? Find the unit rates to prove your answer.
level2.sampleAnswer: The student's reasoning is not valid — getting more items does not mean a lower price per item. Store A: $12 ÷ 5 = $2.40 per notebook. Store B: $20 ÷ 8 = $2.50 per notebook. Store A is actually cheaper per notebook, even though Store B offers more notebooks per purchase.
level2.hint: Remember to show the division you used for each unit price and compare them.
hints: 'More notebooks' and 'cheaper per notebook' are different claims — the question asks you to test the student's shortcut.
Compute both unit prices: dollars ÷ notebooks for each store. Then judge whether the student's reasoning holds.
Store A: divide 12 ÷ 5 for price per notebook. Then compute 20 ÷ 8 for Store B and compare the two prices in your answer.
level2.stemEs: La tienda A vende 5 cuadernos por $12. La tienda B vende 8 cuadernos por $20. Sin calcular, un estudiante dice que la tienda B tiene que ser más barata porque recibes más cuadernos. ¿Es válido su razonamiento? Encuentra las tasas por unidad para comprobar tu respuesta.
level2.explanation: Getting more items does not make a deal cheaper; only the price per item does. Store A works out to $12 ÷ 5 = $2.40 per notebook and Store B to $20 ÷ 8 = $2.50 per notebook, so the reasoning is not valid.
level2.explanationEs: Recibir más artículos no hace que una oferta sea más barata; solo el precio por artículo lo determina. La tienda A da $12 ÷ 5 = $2.40 por cuaderno y la tienda B da $20 ÷ 8 = $2.50 por cuaderno, así que el razonamiento no es válido.
hintsEs: 'Más cuadernos' y 'más barato por cuaderno' son afirmaciones distintas: la pregunta te pide poner a prueba el atajo del estudiante.
Calcula los dos precios unitarios: dólares ÷ cuadernos en cada tienda. Luego juzga si el razonamiento del estudiante se sostiene.
Tienda A: divide 12 ÷ 5 para el precio por cuaderno. Luego calcula 20 ÷ 8 para la Tienda B y compara los dos precios en tu respuesta.

level3.stem: Car A travels 180 miles on 6 gallons. Car B travels 225 miles on 9 gallons. Which car gets better gas mileage?
choices: Car A, at 30 miles per gallon
Car B, at 25 miles per gallon
Car B, because it traveled farther
choiceFeedback: 25 miles per gallon is Car B's rate and it is computed correctly, but 30 is the larger rate.
Car B did travel farther, but it burned more gas doing it. Compare miles PER GALLON.
180 divided by 6 is 30 and 225 divided by 9 is 25, so the two rates differ.
level3.explanation: Car A: 180 ÷ 6 = 30 miles per gallon. Car B: 225 ÷ 9 = 25 miles per gallon. 30 > 25, so Car A gets better mileage.
